title: Away to the South, part 2
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: “For my part, I am content in knowing I am as brave as any beast that ever lived, if not braver,” said the Lion modestly.
“If Dorothy would only be contented to live in the Emerald City,” continued the Scarecrow, “we might all be happy together.”
“But I don’t want to live here,” cried Dorothy. “I want to go to Kansas, and live with Aunt Em and Uncle Henry.”
“Well, then, what can be done?” inquired the Woodman.
The Scarecrow decided to think, and he thought so hard that the pins and needles began to stick out of his brains. Finally he said:
“Why not call the Winged Monkeys, and ask them to carry you over the desert?”
“I never thought of that!” said Dorothy joyfully. “It’s just the thing. I’ll go at once for the Golden Cap.”
When she brought it into the Throne Room she spoke the magic words, and soon the band of Winged Monkeys flew in through the open window and stood beside her.
“This is the second time you have called us,” said the Monkey King, bowing before the little girl. “What do you wish?”
“I want you to fly with me to Kansas,” said Dorothy.
But the Monkey King shook his head.

“That cannot be done,” he said. “We belong to this country alone, and cannot leave it. There has never been a Winged Monkey in Kansas yet, and I suppose there never will be, for they don’t belong there. We shall be glad to serve you in any way in our power, but we cannot cross the desert. Good-bye.”
And with another bow, the Monkey King spread his wings and flew away through the window, followed by all his band.
Dorothy was ready to cry with disappointment. “I have wasted the charm of the Golden Cap to no purpose,” she said, “for the Winged Monkeys cannot help me.”
“It is certainly too bad!” said the tender-hearted Woodman.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the Scarecrow's suggestion?
options: Call the Winged Monkeys to carry her over the desert
Build a second balloon out of green silk
Send for the Queen of the Field Mice
Ask the Guardian of the Gates for advice

questions.prompt: Per the passage, how did the Monkey King answer?
options: That they belong to this country and cannot leave it
That they would carry her but not the dog
That the charm had already been used up
That Kansas lies too far for any flight

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how many times had Dorothy now called the Monkeys?
options: Twice
Once
Three times
She had never called them

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what happened when the Scarecrow thought hard?
options: Pins and needles began to stick out of his brains
His head bulged until Dorothy feared it would burst
He fell over and had to be picked up
He forgot what he had been asked

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Lion describe his own courage?
options: As brave as any beast that ever lived, if not braver
Still very small, whatever Oz had given him
Enough for the city, but not for the woods
Greater than the Winged Monkeys' own

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did Dorothy call the idea just the thing?
options: She had never thought of using the Monkeys that way
She had already tried every other plan
The Scarecrow rarely had any ideas at all
The Golden Cap was about to be taken from her

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does Dorothy conclude after the Monkeys leave?
options: That she has wasted a call of the Golden Cap
That the Monkeys were lying about the desert
That she must walk across the desert herself
That the Scarecrow's brains are no use at all

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what would make the Scarecrow perfectly happy?
options: If Dorothy were content to live in the Emerald City
If Oz came back to rule the city again
If the Winged Monkeys served him as well
If he could return to his own cornfield

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does modestly convey about the Lion?
options: He says it without boasting
He says it in a whisper
He says it doubting it himself
He says it to please the others

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: A good idea is tried at once and refused by those who must obey
The Winged Monkeys carry Dorothy across the desert at last
The Scarecrow persuades Dorothy to remain in the city
A quarrel between Dorothy and the Monkey King

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where did Dorothy want to live?
options: In Kansas, with Aunt Em and Uncle Henry
In the Emerald City with her friends
In the Yellow Castle of the Winkies
In the land of the Quadlings

questions.prompt: Per the passage, how did the Monkeys enter the Throne Room?
options: Through the open window
Through the great front door
Down the chimney of the Palace
They did not enter at all

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Woodman say about the refusal?
options: That it was certainly too bad
That the Monkeys should be forced
That Dorothy should try the charm again
That he had expected it all along

options: To serve her in any way within their power
To carry her as far as the desert's edge
To find someone else who can help her
Nothing whatever; he simply refuses

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why has no Winged Monkey ever been in Kansas?
options: They do not belong there and cannot leave Oz
Nobody has ever asked them to go
The desert is too wide for their wings
Kansas has no forests for them to live in

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does to no purpose mean?
options: Without achieving anything
Without meaning to
Without telling her friends
Without knowing the words

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: A hopeful plan is spent and wasted in a single morning
A hopeful plan carries Dorothy home the same day
The Monkeys agree to take Dorothy as far as they can
The Scarecrow admits his brains were a fraud
